summary: Thermal Orbit is an interactive 3D Earth web app that tracks global wildfires using data from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellites. It solves the problem of scattered satellite data by combining detections from both sensors onto one simple globe with an observation calendar, regional analysis, wildfire stories, and an AI map assistant. This makes complex fire data easy for researchers, emergency teams, and communities to understand and use for faster safety decisions
details:
Thermal Orbit is an interactive 3D globe web app that tracks and visualizes wildfires around the world. It combines active fire data from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS (NOAA-20) satellites into one clear view. Users can pick dates using an observation calendar, check regional fire trends, explore major wildfire stories, and ask questions using a built-in AI map assistant.

Benefits & Impact Satellite data usually comes from separate sources that are hard for everyday users to read. Thermal Orbit brings this data together in one place so researchers, emergency responders, and local communities can easily spot fire hazards and understand wildfire patterns without needing complicated software.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Frontend: JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for the 3D globe and interactive dashboard.
  • Backend: Python and Node.js to fetch and clean the NASA satellite data.
  • Data & AI: NASA FIRMS (MODIS & VIIRS fire datasets) and the Gemini API for the map assistant.

Creativity & Key Considerations Instead of showing plain spreadsheets or flat maps, we combined a 3D Earth view with guided wildfire stories and a smart map assistant that answers questions in plain language. Our team focused on matching data accurately between two different satellites, keeping the 3D map fast and smooth, and making the interface simple for anyone to use.
